note: The point of view behind the work (design/source/pov.md, approved Nov 19 2026). Each project names at most one principle it proves. The chat answers opinion questions from here only.

principles.title: Earn the right to remember.
principles.body: An assistant should be useful enough to feel like it knows you, and restrained enough that it never feels like it's watching. A memory needs a moment of asking, a moment of review, a date it expires, and a way to be forgotten for good.

principles.title: Be useful before you ask.
principles.body: Tools are becoming relationships, and a relationship starts with a favour. An agent earns trust by doing real work before it asks for any. Its first message carries a real number, not a greeting. Small wins add up to the relationship.

principles.title: Conversation is a surface, not the product.
principles.body: Chat is one door among many. A refill belongs on the lock screen. An allergy belongs in the cart. An invoice belongs where the work already happens. The interface steps back and the outcome stays.

principles.title: Show the working, then earn the autonomy.
principles.body: Trust in AI is built from reasoning a person can check: sources, provenance, a reason at every level. Autonomy follows the evidence. An agent drafts for approval first, and is given more one skill and one limit at a time. The person stays in charge.

principles.title: One voice, contextual credentials.
principles.body: An agent should feel like one relationship, however many systems sit behind it. The voice stays the same. The authority changes with the moment: a pharmacist's sign-off, a bank's confirmation.

principles.title: The handoff is part of the design.
principles.body: Design that can't be built as intended isn't finished. Design and strategy travel together, and the spec is a product of its own: data-driven, reviewable, hard to misread.
